subject: Optico Health — Dedicated fleet rightsize request and addendum
messages:
From: Sara Lin <sara@opticohealth.com>
To: dylan.brooks@redwood.ai
Cc: prashant.kumar@opticohealth.com
Date: Sat, 1 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated fleet sizing for renewal — Optico (Q4 commit)

Hi Dylan,

We’re approaching our annual renewal and need to reconcile committed GPUs with actual usage. Q2 spiked but sustained utilization has been ~45% of committed capacity. Before we sign the renewal, can Redwood propose a rightsize option — either a temporary tranche reduction with burst credits during clinical runs, or a swap into a smaller reserved tier?

Attached: optico_usage_report_Q2.csv (hourly utilization), workload_trace_202607.csv (short traces)

Goals:
- Reduce monthly committed GPUs by ~30% while preserving peak coverage
- Maintain latency SLOs for inference (<120ms p50) during daily clinical windows
- Keep path to scale back up quickly (within 48–72 hours)

Can you share a proposal and the operational impacts (scaling lead time, billing proration, SLAs)?

Thanks,
Sara Lin
Head of ML Platform
Optico Health

From: dylan.brooks@redwood.ai
To: Sara Lin <sara@opticohealth.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, dev.patel@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated fleet sizing for renewal — Optico (Q4 commit)

Hi Sara — thanks for the data and call last week.

Quick summary of what we can do:
- Option A: Rightsize commit to 70% of current GPUs (30% reduction) with automatic burst pool for peak windows (max 4x baseline) billed on actuals. 24–48h scale-up lead time to restore full commit.
- Option B: Keep commit but migrate 30% into a lower-cost preemptible tranche for background workloads; guaranteed reserved pool remains for latency-sensitive traffic.
- Option C: Hybrid — smaller commit + 72-hour hot-standby reserves we can warm on demand (adds small monthly fee but reduces overage risk).

Operational notes from infra:
- We can implement proration in the billing for mid-cycle changes; addendum required for commit amendment.
- SLA impact: any reduction of reserved GPUs reduces guaranteed throughput; we’ll put a fallback routing policy to hosted models in case of sustained pressure.

I’ve looped in Marissa for commercial terms and Dev for lead-time / engineering constraints. Expect a draft addendum and a cost comparison by EOD Thu.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
To: Sara Lin <sara@opticohealth.com>, dylan.brooks@redwood.ai
Cc: dev.patel@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 6 Aug 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated fleet sizing for renewal — Optico (Q4 commit)

Sara,

Attached is a proposed addendum (proposed_addendum_v3.pdf) with three commercial paths and the estimated monthly run-rate for each. Highlights:
- Path 1 (Conservative): 0% reduction, add burst credits — minimal contract churn
- Path 2 (Rightsize): 30% reduction in committed GPUs, 2x monthly burst pool, 10% lower monthly commit fee, 1.5x overage multiplier
- Path 3 (Flexible): 30% reduction + 72-hour hot-standby (small reservation fee), ability to revert to prior commit with 48h notice

If Optico signs Path 2 we will: add the addendum, apply prorated credits for the next billing cycle, and schedule a dry-run of scaling on Aug 20 to validate warm-up time.

Can you confirm which path you want by Tue 10 Aug so we can finalize pricing and engineering sched?

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Senior Renewals Manager
Redwood Inference

From: dev.patel@redwood.ai
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, dylan.brooks@redwood.ai
Cc: Sara Lin <sara@opticohealth.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2026 11:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated fleet sizing for renewal — Optico (Q4 commit)

Hi all,

Technical clarifications and timeline:
- Warm-up lead time tests show we can reliably bring a tranche back online in 36 hours (95th pct) for the model family Optico uses (causal-16k variants).
- Burst pool: uses shared spare capacity in-region; cold-start tail adds ~70ms p95 during heavy churn. We’ll provide tracing hooks so Optico can detect fallback and trigger retries client-side.
- Preemptible tranche: not suitable for inference with strict latency SLOs during clinical windows; recommend only for batch/async jobs.

Action items for dry-run Aug 20:
- Redwood infra: schedule warmup on test cluster, capture latency traces
- Optico: provide a short synthetic load (10k tokens/min for 2 hours) and an ops contact to coordinate

I’ll prepare a short runbook post-test and update the addendum with the exact SLA language.

—Dev
Dev Patel
Principal Systems Engineer
Redwood Inference
